findings.evidence: Gotchas: "Never rebase onto local `main` ..., never `git pull` ..., never `git merge` ..." repeats step 3 (line 19): "Rebase onto the remote ref, never local `main`; never `git pull` or `git merge`."
findings.fix: Keep the reasons only in the Gotchas bullet and cut line 19 to "Rebase onto `$base/$target` (see Gotchas). In order:", so the same rule is not loaded twice.

findings.evidence: The principle behind the three rebase forms comes only at the end of step 3(c): "Replaying from the old base keeps only the feature commits." Steps (a) to (c) read as bare conditionals until then.
findings.fix: Open step 3 with the goal: "Replay exactly the commits unique to $branch; fork-point, old_base and plain merge-base are three ways to find that lower boundary, so pick the one that drops no feature commit and carries no rewritten base commit." Then list (a) to (c).

findings.evidence: "`git status --porcelain` not empty: stop, name the uncommitted paths" also matches untracked `??` files. Those files do not block a rebase, so the check stops on harmless scratch files.
findings.fix: Use `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` for the stop check. List untracked files only as a note, unless the rebase later fails because an untracked file would be overwritten (step 4 then reports git's error).

findings.evidence: No branch covers an already up-to-date branch. When `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base/$target" "$branch"` succeeds, the command still asks "This force-pushes <branch>; is it yours alone?" and then runs a no-op rebase and push.
findings.fix: Add to step 2, after the fetch: "If `git merge-base --is-ancestor \"$base/$target\" \"$orig\"` succeeds, report '<branch> already contains <base>/<target>; nothing to rebase or push' and stop before the ownership question."
